name: HomeTube
description: HomeTube is a web UI for yt-dlp that downloads single videos or whole playlists into a clean folder structure for Plex, Jellyfin or Emby. It picks the best AV1/VP9 quality profile automatically, embeds subtitles, chapters and metadata, marks or removes sponsor segments with SponsorBlock, cuts clips, keeps playlists in sync and can trigger a Jellyfin library refresh after each download.

notes.text: HomeTube has no login. Anyone who can reach port 8501 can download to your media folder, so keep it on a trusted network or put it behind a reverse proxy with authentication.

Videos are saved to /opt/hometube_data/videos (VIDEOS_FOLDER), into the destination folder chosen in the UI; playlists get a folder of their own. To write straight into a Plex, Jellyfin or Emby library, bind-mount it there, e.g. pct set <CTID> -mp0 /mnt/media/youtube,mp=/opt/hometube_data/videos, then restart the container. In an unprivileged container the host folder must be writable by UID 100000.

YouTube increasingly needs cookies, even for public videos. Export them with a cookies.txt browser extension and copy the file to /opt/hometube_data/cookies/youtube_cookies.txt, then reload the HomeTube page so it switches to file cookies.

Settings such as LANGUAGE_PRIMARY, VIDEO_QUALITY_MAX, YTDLP_CUSTOM_ARGS or JELLYFIN_BASE_URL/JELLYFIN_API_KEY go in /opt/hometube_data/.env, then run systemctl restart hometube. Temporary files are removed after each download (REMOVE_TMP_FILES_AFTER_DOWNLOAD=true) so videos are not stored twice; set it to false to keep them as a re-download cache.
yt-dlp updates itself on every HomeTube restart and with every update run, since YouTube breaks older versions regularly. YouTube challenges are solved with the installed deno.
